prompt: Since the 14:05 deploy of api-gateway v2.31, edge clients are getting a flood of 429s -- error rate on the /v1/orders path jumped from 0.2% to 18%. The release notes say the limiter config was not touched. Stop the storm.

Our payments-api token-bucket limiter is rejecting ~90% of requests even at low traffic (80 rps against a documented 600 rps cap). This started after we migrated the limiter config from the old limits.yaml to the new limits.toml last night.

When notification-worker gets throttled by our SMS provider, our outbound error rate snowballs from a few 429s into a full 5-minute outage. The provider returns Retry-After: 30 but we appear to keep hammering them.

Customers on the 100 req/min plan can intermittently push ~190 requests in a few seconds and our DB sees the spike, even though the limiter reports them 'within limit'. It clusters right around the top of each minute.

Our distributed limiter runs on 6 gateway pods sharing one Redis counter. Since this morning, allowed throughput oscillates +/-40% minute-to-minute and some pods reject identically-keyed traffic that others let through. No deploy went out.
Every tenant is suddenly getting 429s on our shared 10k req/min ingestion bucket, and P99 for everyone jumped from 80ms to timeouts at 13:20. Tenant acme-prod (api_key ...7f3a) looks unusually busy.

We set a generous burst of 5000 on the search-api token bucket (steady 500/s) to absorb spikes, but every few hours a thundering herd of cron clients drains the whole burst at once and our Elasticsearch cluster red-flags with a query-queue overflow.

The circuit breaker protecting inventory-svc is flapping -- it opens, half-opens, sends one probe, trips back open, repeating every ~10s, and we keep shedding 70% of traffic. Downstream actually recovered minutes ago. This began after we tuned breaker thresholds yesterday.

ingest-pipeline pods are OOMKilled every ~20 minutes under load. Heap dumps show millions of queued messages. We added rate limiting on the HTTP intake, but the in-memory work queue between the handler and the DB writer looks unbounded.

Our Redis-backed sliding-window limiter intermittently lets clients blow far past their limits -- one client did 4x their 1000/min cap at 02:00. Redis memory has sat near maxmemory all week. No limiter code changed.

pdf-render-svc uses a concurrency limiter capped at 50 in-flight jobs. Over a few hours, effective concurrency creeps down to single digits and eventually 0 -- all requests block -- until we restart the pod. Throughput dies even though CPU is idle.

After the HPA scaled checkout-api from 4 to 16 pods during a flash sale, upstream tax-svc got hammered with 4x its agreed 2000 rps and started shedding. Each checkout pod's limiter is configured to exactly 500 rps toward tax-svc, which 'looks correct'.

Our graphql-gateway enforces a 10000 cost-units/min budget per client, but a few clients running deeply-nested queries are melting the DB despite showing only ~30% budget used. Simple and expensive queries seem to cost the same.

We front email-dispatch with a leaky-bucket limiter to smooth sends to our SMTP relay. Since we raised the bucket size last week, end-to-end send latency climbed from 2s to 90s and the bucket is always full, though we are dropping nothing.
